about: Chiamare il Re (Torino 1787, «Del giuoco, che dicesi volgarmente chiamare il Re», pp. 79-84), a game for four that the book describes in passing: dealt as Permesso for four (19 cards, the dealer puts two away), the dealer, who has «un doppio vantaggio», calls any king and its secret holder is his partner, two against two, who count together to 46 points «dedotta la carta del Folle» (pp. 80-81). If he holds all four kings he may call a queen, with all kings and queens a knight, with all of those a jack (pp. 81-82). The dealer may instead go alone, changing one card («ad una») or none («sans prendre»), against the other three; another player may take the «ad una» first (p. 82). The payments are «secondo il convenuto» (p. 83): the book names no figure. The pages do not say what happens with a king in the dealer's own discard (it cannot arise: rule 38 bars the kings, [R]; a queen, a knight or a jack may lie there and is then not called either), nor who leads (the general rule of p. 35, [R]); the case of four kings and four queens with a queen in the discard is read on the hand alone, as written at the ladder (about one hand in 115,000).

dummett1980.cite: Michael Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London: Duckworth, 1980, chapter XIII «Tarocco in Piedmont and Lombardy», pp. 258-279 (our scan is partial: printed page 268 is missing)

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

prammatica1846.cite: L. B., Prammatica del giuocatore di tarocchi ossia regole indispensabili per gli amatori di simile passatempo, Torino, Serra, [1846] (separate issue, cover dated 1846, deposited 27 December 1845; reprinted from the same setting, same pages, as part II of Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, Torino, Serra, [1846])

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 79: «Siffatto giuoco usasi giuocare in quattro persone».

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right.

first_dealer.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 16 (general rule): cards are turned up and «se viene prima da questa parte un Trionfo, mischierò io». General rule of the book, not repeated in the section.

cut_by.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 16-17 (general rule): «di dar a coppare a chi ti siede a sinistra»: the player on the dealer's left cuts. General rule of the book, not repeated in the section; p. 58 (Permesso, said before the deal) has only «ed a sinistra coppati».

cut_min.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: the page forbids only a cut of one card; that each part keeps at least two cards is our reading.

dealer_rotation.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 70: after a hand that «si deve ripigliar da capo» «tocca al compagno appresso a mischiare, e dar i Tarocchi»: the next player deals; the book names no other change of dealer, and «appresso» is read in the direction of play (to the right).

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 80-83: with a called king two against two («di due giuocatori contra altri due»); alone, one against three («gli altri tre compagni tuoi uniti insieme»).

pool.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 81-83: «conteranno insieme i loro punti»; the three against the lone player «conteranno tra loro tre i loro punti unitamente».

signals.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 73: knocks and signs are barred «a chiamare il Re».

deck.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 79: dealt «come a pag. 71»; 4 × 19 + 2 = 78 (the numbers are not printed on p. 79).

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 9-10, 13: the trionfi rank by their printed numbers, with the Angel XX above the World XXI («l'usanza, che in questo caso fa legge»); checked on the scan on 2 November 2026.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: swords and batons run 10 down to 1, cups and coins 1 up to 10, the courts above every numeral in the order King, Queen, Knight, Jack; checked on the scan on 2 November 2026.

card_points.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14, 51: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, the Angel, the Bagatto and the Fool 5, every other card 1 in the book's numbers; checked on the scan on 2 November 2026.

fool.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 79-84 do not say how the Fool plays; ours: as in the other games of the book (it is shown, takes nothing).

fool_exchange.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 81: the 46 are counted «dedotta la carta del Folle». Torino [1846], part I, p. 39, the same game: the card deducted is the one «che dassi in compenso del Folle».

fool_exchange_to.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 33 (Venticinque for three, another game): to «chi ha presa o coperta la mano»; carried over to this game, whose pages do not say it.

fool_exchange_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 52: «una cartaccia, qualunque gli piaccia», and Torino [1846], part I, p. 33: «un'altra cartuccia qualunque»: the owner chooses the plain card he gives; carried over to this game, whose pages (pp. 79-84) do not repeat it. Venticinque and Morto give the cheapest card instead (question 18).

replace.what: who chooses the card given for the Fool

fool_no_tricks.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 21, rule 10, lists among the things to be agreed before the deal whether a player «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto» loses the «vola»: it supposes that a player with no trick may hold the Fool, so the Fool stays with him. The pages of this game (pp. 79-84) do not say what a player with no trick does with the Fool, and they do not send to p. 50. Our reading: a player with no trick keeps the Fool; an owner without a plain card gives nothing. Other reading (alt give_fool): Prammatica [1846], p. 6: «chi non potesse coprirlo, alla fine della mano è obbligato di cederlo alla parte vincente»; Torino 1880, p. 9 says only that the Fool of a side with no trick may be taken («as peul piesse»); Dummett 1980, p. 259: «if they have won no tricks, they must surrender the Folle». See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 2.

replace.what: the Fool of a player who won no trick: kept or given up

options.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 83: «secondo il convenuto»; the sums are settled before the deal as in the general rule of p. 21 («Tutto questo si dee concludere chiaramente prima di dare le carte»); the choices offered here are ours, the book names no figure.

contracts.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 80-81: the dealer calls a king; its holder is his partner: «affinchè egli abbia un compagno».
[D] Torino 1787, p. 82: «andar solo, chiamando una carta, e dandone via un'altra coperta in tavola»; «ad una».
[D] Torino 1787, pp. 82, 84: «Io vado à sans prendre»; «O si vada ad una, od a sans prendre».

hand_size.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 38, of this game: «Si danno diciannove carte a ciascuno». Torino 1787, p. 79 sends to p. 71 («dieciannove»): «Dansi eguali carte a ciascuno de' giuocatori, come a pag. 71.»

dealer_extra.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 71, 79-80: «scartansi pure, come ivi dicemmo, due sole carte»: the dealer has two over (4 × 19 + 2 = 78; his 21 is not printed).

packets.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59 (Permesso): the way of dealing is the dealer's, announced before the cut.

packets_announced.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 59: announced before the cut; this game sends to p. 71 for the deal.

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 79-80: «scartansi pure … due sole carte»; «chi mischia, e dà le carte, ha un doppio vantaggio, cioè quello dello scarto».

who.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 80: the discard is the dealer's advantage.

count_mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 79-80: «due sole carte»: exactly two. Other reading: at most two, as Torino [1846], part I, p. 38 says of this game: «non può scartarne più di due» (the same words in Torino 1787, p. 71, Permesso for four).

discard_honours_barred.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 34 (general rule 38): the honours are not put away; the Re pages (79-84) do not repeat it.

allowed_exceptions.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 34 (rule 38): «eccetto che Bagatto sia solo, senza il Folle»: «solo» is read as the only trump of the hand, as Dummett 1980, p. 259 reads this rule («neither the Folle nor any other trump»). Revision 1 read it as «holding no Fool». The exception for the Fool «in un sol caso … vola» is not played (see left_out). Other reading: no exception, as the rules of 1830 have it (Dummett, p. 259).

counts_for.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 21, rule 10 (for every game), lists among the things to be agreed before the deal whether a player «avendo o il Folle, o lo scarto» loses the «vola»: it supposes that a player with no trick may keep his discard, and no Turin book prints the contrary for a game with one discard. Pages 79-84 do not say whose points the discard joins; ours: the dealer's side. Other reading: a side with no trick gives the discard to the taker of the last trick. That a player with no trick loses his discard is printed only in Prammatica [1846], pp. 24-25, n. 15 «Mittigati in due collo scarto compito», a game for two: «La così detta vola … perde i punti dei due scarti, tanto piccolo che grande», and the Fool with them («e con essi anche il Folle»); the page does not say who gains them. Dummett 1980, p. 259 gives a rule for it («they must surrender the discarded cards to the player or side winning the last trick») and names no source. See OPEN_QUESTIONS.md, question 1.

replace.what: the discard of a player who won no trick: kept or lost

announce.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 60, 72 (Permesso): «Ho scartato» is said before the calling.

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 80-82: after the discard the dealer calls a king, or goes alone; another player may answer «Ad una vado io».

contracts.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 84: «O si vada ad una, od a sans prendre»: two or three cards may not be called, «diversamente egli è subito il giuoco di Permesso».

opens.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 80, 82: only the dealer calls and may go alone: «chi mischia, e dà le carte».

dealer_speaks.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 80-82: «chiamasi un Re solamente da chi ha date le carte»; the others answer his declaration.

tie.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 82: «Se un altro tuo compagno poi ti … pare: Io vado à sans prendre»: the dealer has only these two ways out, so on an equal bid the other player goes (the second reading takes it as [D]). The page gives the equal bid only for «ad una» («Ad una vado io» takes the dealer's «ad una»); that another player may also equal the dealer's «sans prendre» is our extension: the page does not say it (see open question 35). Other reading: the dealer keeps his equal bid.

after_dealer_pass.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 80, 82: the dealer speaks first; if he does not go alone he «chiama qualunque Re» (p. 80), and another player may answer a bid of the dealer with «Ad una vado io» (p. 82). Read: the dealer's pass ends the auction and he calls a King; the others may only overcall a bid of the dealer, or match it (bidding.tie). Other reading: after the dealer passes the others may still bid.

replace.what: the auction after the dealer passes

overbid_returns.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 82: «Se un altro tuo compagno poi ti risponderà: Ad una vado io», then «tu o lo lascierai andare, o risponderai … Io vado à sans prendre»: the second reading gives the dealer the word at once after another player's answer (to let him go, or to bid «sans prendre»); played: the word goes on in the order of speech. The page prints no further turn after the answer. By the letter of p. 82 the word goes back to the dealer (this is our alt); about the two other players the page is silent. Torino [1846], part I, p. 39 reprints the same text: it is not a second witness.

replace.what: who has the word after a raise in the auction

all_pass.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 80: if nobody goes alone the dealer «chiama qualunque Re, il quale più gli piaccia, e convenga».

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 80-83: the dealer calls a king after the discard.

caller.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 80: «chiamasi un Re solamente da chi ha date le carte».

ladder.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 81-82: all four kings → a queen; kings and queens → a knight; kings, queens and knights → a jack: «potrà chiamare una Donna, … non mai un … Donne insieme coi Re». [S] If the caller holds all sixteen courts and no card of the ladder can be called, he plays alone as at sans prendre: the book is silent (pp. 81-82); ours.

step_down.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 81-82: only when he holds all four of the rank below. For the kings the page says «in mano» after the discard (p. 81: «Chi avendo già scartato, troverassi in mano tutti i quattro Re»); for the queens and the rest «in the hand» is our reading, and «in the hand and the discard together» is the other. The case of four kings and four queens with a queen in the discard (about one hand in 115,000) is read on the hand alone: the dealer may then call only a queen of his own hand. Recorded, not changed.

secret.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 80: the holder «starà ben cheto, e non darà indizio veruno di averlo».

own_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 83 prints that one who calls a card he holds himself plays alone, unless all the others forgive him, «ma da tutti i compagni, dico concordemente». The table allows the call; it stays secret, like any call, until that card is played, and the caller plays alone against three; Not played: the forgiveness of the three is not built (see left_out own_card_forgiveness); the others cannot know the card is his. Torino [1846], part I, p. 40: «dovrai andar solo senza altra chiamata»; it names no forgiveness. Other versions: the three are asked to forgive; or the table does not offer a card the caller holds (the book calls it a «fallo» of one who «non l'avesse veduto», p. 83).

replace.what: calling a card of one's own hand

card_in_discard.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 80-81 do not say what happens when the called king lies in the dealer's own discard. By rule 38 (p. 34: «Nessun onore, cioè nessun Re … si potrà scartare»; the same in Torino [1846], part I, p. 16) no king is put away, so for a king the case does not arise. A queen, a knight or a jack may be put away (rule 38 bars the honours only); the engine does not let the dealer call a card of his own discard, whatever its rank: not allowed. Other reading: he plays alone.

replace.what: the payment when a King is called; a called King in the discard

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 82: «Farai insomma un cambio d'una carta sola sulle regole del Permesso».

lay_down_first.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 82: «sulle regole del Permesso» (pp. 64-66): the card is laid down before the calling.

face.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 82: «dandone via un'altra coperta in tavola».

callable.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 82: «chiamando una carta»: any card, as at Permesso.

card_not_held.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 82 does not say what happens when the called card is in the dealer's discard; ours as in Permesso for three.

give.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 39, of this game: the laid card is «ritirata da chi ti avrà dato la carta chiamata». Here one card is exchanged, so random gives the same: the holder of the called card takes the one laid card. Torino 1787, p. 82 plays the exchange «sulle regole del Permesso» (p. 61). Other version: the declarer hands them out as he likes.

discard_honours_barred.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 34-35 (general rule 38): no honour, «nessun Re, nè l'Angelo, nè il Folle, nè Bagatto», may be put away, but «Si potrà però il Folle dar via … ove si giuochi a Permesso». Read: the cards laid down in the exchange are put away like a discard, so the kings, the Angel and Bagatto may not be laid down; the Fool may. Other reading: the bar is for the discard only and any card may be laid down.

replace.what: which cards may be laid down in the exchange

allowed_exceptions.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 34-35: «Si potrà però il Folle dar via … ove si giuochi a Permesso»: the Fool may be laid down in the exchange. The exception of a lone Bagatto (p. 34) is said of the discard and is not carried over.

first_leader.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 35 (general rule): «Chi è a destra di chi dà, comincia»; pp. 79-84 do not say who leads, so the general rule is carried over. Other reading: the lone player leads.

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 37: «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la mano … deve essere il primo a giuocare».

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 35: «debbon rispondere con carte della medesima sequenza».

must_trump.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36, for Partita and «anche negli altri giuochi»: «si risponderà e prenderà con un Trionfo». Torino 1787, p. 36 only shows it. Torino 1787, p. 49 (Baronetti) prints the same duty: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi».

must_overtrump.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 36-37: no duty to beat the trump on the table.

fool_may_lead.source: [S] Ours: the book does not say whether the Fool may be led.

count_unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 51-52: «ogni carta dee essere accompagnata con un'altra carta»; 46 (p. 81); 91 is our sum.

group.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 81: 46 points reads as the pairs of p. 52; the Re pages name no counting step.

odd_card.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 54: an unpaired card counts, as at Venticinque.

fool_card.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 81: «quarantasei, dedotta la carta del Folle». Torino [1846], part I, p. 39, the same game: the 46 are counted after the compensation card is given.

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 81: «i quali per guadagnar la partita debbono ascendere a quarantasei».

tie.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 74, 79: the game is dealt «come a pag. 71» and at four «non si può mai rifare per eguaglianza di punti»; ours: the side that does not make 46 loses, nothing is replayed. The 46 of a lone player against three is not printed (read the same).

game_points.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 82-83: the hand is settled in stakes («secondo il convenuto»).

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 83: «secondo il convenuto»: the agreed sum.

mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 90 (Partita, two against two): each winner collects from one opponent; the Re pages name no mode for two against two; read the same. [S] When the caller called a card of his own and plays alone against three, the same amount is paid to or from each of the three, as declarer_vs_each; ours.

amount.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 82-83 print the payment only for the lone player («secondo il convenuto»); for two against two it is not said; ours: the simple stake agreed before the deal.

replace.what: the payment when a King is called; a called King in the discard

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 83: «secondo il convenuto»: the agreed sum.

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 82-83: «tu sarai obbligato a pagarli tutti, secondo … a pagar te, secondo il convenuto»: to and from each of the three.

amount.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 82-83: «secondo il convenuto»; the book names no figure. The simple stake agreed before the deal (option stake). This game has no «a due» (Torino 1787, p. 84).

kind.source: [S] Ours: the book describes one hand and its stakes; they are settled after every hand, the match ends after one round of dealers (match.dealer_rounds); the greatest balance wins, equal balances are a draw («pace»).

dealer_rounds.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 79-84 are silent on the length of a match: the book describes one hand and its payment. Ours: one round of dealers, four hands, each player dealing once; the payments are made after every hand and the greatest balance wins. The table may agree on two or three rounds.

effect.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 83 prints that one who calls a card of his own plays alone against the three, unless all forgive him («dico concordemente»). Applied by the table when that card is played; forgiveness is not offered (the others cannot know the card is his). Other versions: see hand.call_partner.own_card.

replace.what: calling a card of one's own hand

effect.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 83: «Chi desse al compagno un qualche indizio … semplice, e pura maniera del giuoco»; «questi» is the holder of the king who gave the hint (second reading); other reading: the dealer.

[D] Torino 1787, p. 73: «costui pagherà la partita semplice a tutti … giuocare, o far cessare il giuoco»; named for Permesso for three, four and five and for Chiamare il Re (and «a qualunque altro giuoco di Tarocchi»). [R] who the offender may be is not said (any player); the table cannot see a knock, so only the rules page tells it.

[D] Torino 1787, pp. 33-34 (rule 35; p. 38 sends to it, said for Sedici; p. 79 (Meno) and p. 90 (Partita) send to it): «incorrere nella pena accennata … num. 35. di … tutti i giuocatori compagni»; the engine refuses a card that does not follow suit.

bid.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 84: «Per andare a solo … almen otto Trionfi, … è facilissimo a perdere». This is a piece of advice; the condition holds only the first part (eight trumps), the format has room for one count.

left_out.source: [R] Dummett 1980, p. 269 (our scan lacks page 268): a basic payment of 2 for «ad una»; only the 1 for calling a king is his conjecture. His 1 for «a due» belongs to Permesso: this game has none (Torino 1787, p. 84: «col chiamare due, o tre carte, non potrà mai»). Prammatica [1846], p. 17, later, lets the Permesso on one or two cards be agreed (see permesso_one_or_two_cards).
left_out.why: Not printed in the 1787 book; the payment is the agreed stake.

left_out.source: [D] Prammatica [1846], p. 17: «Il Permesso ad una o due carte, secondo che si stabilisce» must be asked «prima che lo scarto sia divenuto alla dimanda del Re»; p. 16: the king called «sarà obbligato di farsi conoscere appena lo possa».
left_out.why: Later than the book of 1787, which differs: p. 84 lets the dealer go alone only «ad una» or «sans prendre», never with two or three cards («col chiamare due, o tre carte, non potrà mai»), and p. 80 has the holder of the called king keep silent («starà ben cheto»). The Prammatica allows one or two cards by agreement and makes the king show himself. Not played; the file follows the book of 1787.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 34 (rule 38): the Fool may be put away «in un sol caso … guadagnar la partita vola».
left_out.why: Vola is not played (open question 13); the exception is not offered.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 83: «se non gli verrà da tutti il fallo passato per buono» (all the partners, «dico concordemente»), then «egli allora sarà tenuto ad andar solo senza altra chiamata».
left_out.why: Not played: the partners cannot know that the called card is the caller's own, so nobody can be asked to forgive; the caller plays alone (penalties.call_own_card, hand.call_partner.own_card).
